headline: Revenue and margins surge on broad-based demand strength
summary_short: Cognex's Q1 2026 revenue rose 24.3% y/y (+6.4% q/q) to $268M on broad-based demand across major end markets, with gross margin expanding to 71% from 67% and diluted EPS more than doubling y/y to $0.31 from $0.14.
summary_long: Revenue grew 24% y/y (6% q/q) to $268.4M on broad-based demand across major end markets, led by consumer electronics, semiconductor, and logistics customers, plus favorable FX translation. Gross margin expanded to 71% from 67% y/y on favorable mix and higher-volume cost efficiencies, partly offset by tariffs. Operating income rose to 22% of revenue from 12% on operating leverage; net income more than doubled y/y to $51.7M, or $0.31 diluted EPS versus $0.14. Cognex completed the divestiture of its Japan-focused trading business (Moritex) for $12.0M, booking a $1.5M pretax loss. Cash fell to $237.3M from $262.9M q/q on $99.0M of buybacks and a $14.2M dividend payment; the company carries no long-term debt.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth broadened across all four regions and end markets, gross margin expanded on favorable mix and volume efficiencies, and operating leverage pushed operating income to 22% of revenue from 12% a year earlier.

Broad-based demand across consumer electronics, semiconductor, packaging, and logistics customers in all four regions, plus a weaker U.S. dollar versus the Euro and Renminbi, drove the 24% y/y increase.
More favorable end-market mix and cost efficiencies from higher sales volume lifted gross margin to 71% from 67%, partly offset by tariff impact.
Operating leverage from the revenue increase pushed operating income to 22% of revenue from 12%, even as incentive-compensation accruals and reorganization charges raised opex 11%.

EBITDA tracks operating income's operating-leverage gain; the depreciation and amortization add-back (about $7.2M) was roughly flat versus the prior quarter, so the two metrics move in near lock-step.
Net income scaled with the 122% rise in pretax income (operating leverage plus higher investment income); the effective tax rate ticked up to 16% from 15%, aided by a $1.2M discrete tax benefit.
EPS rose in step with net income; diluted share count fell 1.2% y/y on continued buybacks, adding a small further per-share tailwind beyond the income gain.
Cost of revenue grew 8% against 24% revenue growth, consistent with the gross-margin expansion to 71% from 67% already explained by mix and volume efficiencies.
Pretax income rose in line with operating income's gain, tempered by a smaller FX loss and a one-time $1.5M pretax loss on the Moritex trading-business divestiture booked in other expense.
Operating cash inflow increased mainly on stronger business performance, partly offset by higher company bonus payments that are made each year in the first quarter.
Cash fell q/q as $99.0M of buybacks and $14.2M of dividends outpaced operating cash inflow; the y/y gain reflects twelve months of cumulative cash generation since the prior-year quarter.
Equity dipped q/q as buybacks and dividends ($99.0M and $14.2M) outweighed $51.7M of net income; the y/y increase shows cumulative earnings outpacing capital returned to shareholders.
Share count fell 1.2% y/y as the $500M buyback program, which repurchased 2,375,000 shares for $99.0M this quarter, outpaced new share issuance under employee stock plans.
